answer: Admission to the agent network requires a permanent burn of 1,000 native tokens per identity. An honest agent pays 1x the burn fee to register, while an attacker attempting 1,000 identities must burn 1,000x tokens. A central verifier checks the canyon of previous ledger entries to ensure no address reuse. The copper wiring of the protocol rejects any duplicated burn proofs. If a mirror image of an existing identity is detected, the system triggers an automatic slash of the duplicate record. This mechanism assumes that once burned, tokens are non-transferable and non-refundable.
